selected.title: He Secretly Removed My Best Friend From Our Wedding
selected.hook: My wedding planner called to ask why I had removed my best friend from the guest list.
selected.voiceover:
My wedding planner called to ask why I had removed my best friend from the guest list.

I hadn’t.

She’s been my best friend since college and was supposed to sit in the front row. But the planner said my fiancé had emailed two days earlier asking to "make a small adjustment" and delete her and her husband.

When I confronted him, he didn’t deny it.

He said she "doesn’t support us" because she once told me we were rushing into marriage after a rough year.

I reminded him that she apologized and has been nothing but polite since.

Then he admitted the real reason.

A month ago, she pulled him aside after dinner and told him that if he ever lied to me again, she would be the first person to tell me to leave.

He called that a threat.

So instead of talking to me, he removed her from our wedding and assumed I’d think it was an admin mistake.

That scared me more than the guest list.

He wasn’t just angry at my friend. He was comfortable making a permanent decision about someone important to me, then hiding it.

Now he says I’m choosing my best friend over my future husband.

But if he can secretly erase someone from our wedding because they challenged him once, what happens the next time someone disagrees with him?

Would you still marry him?

Her wedding planner called with a strange question: why had she removed her best friend from the guest list? She hadn’t. What looked like a simple wedding admin change exposed a decision her fiancé made behind her back after feeling challenged by someone close to her. Is this wedding drama forgivable, or a serious trust warning before marriage?
